note: Built from news coverage and county/city announcements. Not every Florida department is listed yet; departments are added as they show up in the news.

departments.name: Kissimmee Fire Department
departments.detail: First Central Florida department on 24/72. Started April 25, 2026 after hiring 49 firefighters, paid for with a new fire assessment fee.

departments.name: Pasco County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Launched its D-shift (24 on / 72 off) in January 2026.

departments.name: Gainesville Fire Rescue
departments.detail: City approved 24/72 in November 2023 with a target start of mid-2024.

departments.name: Levy County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Adopted 24/72 for firefighters and paramedics in a new three-year contract (September 2025).

departments.name: Lake County Fire Rescue (EMS only)
departments.detail: Paramedics and EMTs moved to 24/72 in August 2025. Firefighters are not yet included (see In talks).

departments.name: Marion County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Contract approved June 2, 2026. County must reach 24/72 by Sept. 30, 2029, hiring nearly 250 people for a new D-shift. Chief hopes to get there sooner.

departments.name: Polk County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: Tentative agreement for a D-shift (24/72) reached July 2026, targeting Oct. 1, 2027. Staffing up with 75 positions added in 2024 and 50 SAFER-funded positions. Final commission vote still pending.

departments.name: St. Johns County Fire Rescue
departments.detail: IAFF Local 3865 is pushing for 24/72 plus about 125 hires. Talks went to impasse in January 2026 and were still in the state impasse process as of May 2026.

departments.name: Lake County Fire Rescue (firefighters)
departments.detail: IAFF Local 3990 is working to move dual-certified firefighter/paramedics onto the same 24/72 schedule EMS staff already have.

departments.name: Orlando Fire Department
departments.detail: A 42-hour week was a key issue in 2025 bargaining (a fourth platoon would need about 135 more firefighters). The November 2025 contract kept a 48-hour week, so it remains a future goal.
